summary: Fail closed on interrupted allocation and malformed host inputs, preserve root glob matches

delivery.outcome: Stop interrupted ticket allocation after cleanup, reject control-character titles before effects and serialize JSON safely, reject malformed or duplicate managed host paragraphs while preserving user text, and match root-level files under whole-segment recursive globs in immutable standard 0.20.64.
nonGoals: Mutate actual user-host files during tests or clean foreign work
Change closed natural-language intent semantics or add runtime dependencies

architecture.decision: Use EXIT cleanup with explicit SIGINT/SIGTERM termination; validate ASCII controls before allocation and use the existing Python JSON serializer for scalars. Reject duplicate or malformed managed headings before pointer replacement. Treat a whole **/ segment as zero or more complete directories while preserving other glob semantics. Verify actual CLI effects, extracted managed pointer logic and actual runtime glob matching. Before first material implementation, the accepted plan includes explicit cross-platform regression CI wiring with ten implementation files and a one-path workflow interface budget.
interfaceChanges: Run runtime boundary regressions in the existing Linux and Windows workflow jobs; POSIX signal checks are explicitly platform-scoped.
architecture.rollback: Revert the material source fix through protected publication; preserve controller and review receipts.

validation.evidence: Actual allocator subprocess signal and title cases stop before reservation/materialization; Unicode remains valid; malformed/duplicate pointers retain user bytes and fail; whole-segment recursive globs match root and nested files without broadening simple-star matches. Original code reproduces four defects.
Existing host and governance suites, parity, native gate and exact-head Linux/Windows/OneDev checks pass.
Independent exact-head protected merge and final immutable standard v0.20.64 release are verified.
